column1: # Proto-Indo-European, as reconstructed for roughly 4000 BCE.
# Laryngeals are given phonetic values: h₁ = h, h₂ = χ, h₃ = ɣʷ.
# Palatovelars ḱ ǵ ǵʰ are kʲ gʲ gʲʱ; "voiced aspirates" are breathy b̤ d̤ ɡʱ.
# Syllabic resonants r̥ l̥ m̥ n̥ are r̩ l̩ m̩ n̩. The accent is marked (ˈ).
# Nouns are stems (thematic stems end in -o); verbs are roots or present
# stems. Only concepts with a widely accepted reconstruction are listed
# (Mallory & Adams 2006; Ringe 2006; LIV²); the rest are coined.

column2: The reconstructed ancestor of the Indo-European languages: laryngeals, breathy stops, a free accent, rich case endings.
Mallory & Adams, The Oxford Introduction to Proto-Indo-European (2006); Ringe (2006); LIV² — simplified by hand
